nodes.name: Epoxide route precipitation
nodes.procedure: Samples were obtained by employing the Epoxide Route. Typically, precipitations were driven by aging for 24–72 h at room temperature aqueous solution adjusted (with HCl solution) at an initial pH around 2 to guarantee the cations' solubility (especially in the case of FeIII). Total cation concentrations, defined as [Ni2+] + [Fe3+], ranged from 15 to 750 mM with Ni:Fe ratio of 2:1. Total chloride concentration [Cl-] = 2[NiII] + 3[FeIII] + [NaCl] was modulated from 40 to 2000 mM by adding NaCl solution. Glycidol (Gly) was added to the aqueous solution under permanent magnetic stirring (Gly concentrations 40-2000 mM), which starts the reaction via nucleophilic attack of chloride ions on the epoxide ring, generating hydroxide ions homogeneously. After precipitation, solids were isolated by filtration or centrifugation, washed 3x with water (50% initial volume) then EtOH, dried at room temperature, and stored in desiccators.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: In a typical synthesis of NiFe-LDH, the nitrate salts of the metals were mixed with TEA and dissolved in 50 ml of degassed Milli-Q water to obtain a final solution with a total metal cation concentration of 20 mM, maintaining a fixed Ni to Fe molar ratio of 2:1. The TEA concentration was adjusted based on the amount of Fe present. Next, 50 ml of a 35 mM aqueous urea solution was added, with the amount of urea corresponding to 75% of the total metal concentration. The resulting dark brown solution was transferred to a 125 mL stainless steel autoclave lined with Teflon and heated in a preheated oven at 120 °C for 48 h. After the reaction period, the autoclave was allowed to cool to room temperature on the bench. The obtained yellowish fine powder was collected by filtration, washed thoroughly with Milli-Q water, and dried under vacuum.

nodes.name: Urea hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.75 mmol), Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (0.25 mmol), and CO(NH2)2 (5 mmol) were dissolved in 36 mL distilled water and stirred to form clear solution. Solution transferred to 125 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave, sealed, maintained at 120°C for 12 h, cooled naturally to room temperature. Final powder filtered, washed several times with Milli-Q water and EtOH, dried 24 h under vacuum at room temperature.

nodes.characterization_summary: RT-NiFe-LDH exhibits very low crystallinity with broad (103) and (110) reflections confirming LDH phase; (003) peak absent indicating mono/bilayer structures; crystallite domains <5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The RT-NiFe-LDH sample exhibits very low crystallinity ... crystalline domains smaller than 5 nm are obtained suggesting the formation of nano-LDHs.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES confirms NiII and FeIII oxidation states in RT-NiFe-LDH matching typical NiFe-LDH catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XANES measurements confirm the occurrence of NiII and FeIII (see dashed vertical lines in Fig. 2b, c).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms NiII (Ni 2p3/2 at 855.8 eV, Ni 2p1/2 at 873.3 eV), FeIII (Fe 2p3/2 at 711.8 eV, Fe 2p1/2 at 723.6 eV); Ni:Fe ratio 2:1, Cl:Fe ratio 1:1; Fe signals suggest defective environments and clustering.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of NiII is supported by the main peaks at 855.8 eV (Ni 2p3/2) and 873.3 eV (Ni 2p1/2) ... Overall, XPS confirms the quantitative incorporation of the cation (Ni:Fe ratio 2:1) and chloride (Cl:Fe ratio 1:1) into the solid phases.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge EXAFS shows third signal at 3.2 Å indicating Fe-Fe pairs and high Fe-clustering; higher Debye-Waller factor confirms structural disorder.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Remarkably, the RT-NiFe-LDH at the Fe K-edge revealed the existence of a third signal at ca. 3.2 Å ... suggesting a high degree of Fe-clustering in the structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: 4K Mössbauer shows magnetic sextets with average Bhf ~50.1 T (vs 40.8 T for HT-NiFe-LDH); ~70% Fe atoms in highest Bhf components confirming higher Fe-clustering.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The higher average Bhf observed in RT-NiFe-LDH (~50.1 T) compared to HT-NiFe-LDH (~40.8 T) supports the presence of more Fe-rich local environments.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows flower-like structures for Ni hydroxides and highly aggregated flakes for RT-NiFe-LDH; typical microparticle agglomerates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: These findings align with the characteristic flower-like structures commonly associated with Ni-based hydroxides, corroborated by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) characterization.
